title: Zero‐sum beliefs and system justification: The roles of perceived involutionary climate and perceived legitimacy of involutionary behaviour
abstract: Abstract Zero‐sum beliefs reflect a win‐lose worldview in which one party's gains are perceived as another party's losses. Although these beliefs are known to undermine interpersonal and intergroup relations, their implications for evaluations of broader social systems remain underexplored. The present research examines how zero‐sum beliefs relate to system justification, focusing on the mediating role of perceived involutionary climate and the moderating role of perceived legitimacy of involutionary behaviour. In Study 1, a cross‐sectional survey ( N = 546) examined associations among zero‐sum beliefs, system justification, perceived involutionary climate, and perceived legitimacy of involutionary behaviour. Study 2 ( N = 260) experimentally manipulated zero‐sum beliefs to further test the proposed mediation and moderation processes. Zero‐sum beliefs were negatively associated with system justification in Study 1, and experimentally induced zero‐sum beliefs resulted in lower system justification in Study 2. In both studies, perceived involutionary climate mediated this relationship, and the indirect effect was weaker when involutionary behaviour was perceived as more legitimate. These findings shed light on how zero‐sum beliefs may shape individuals' evaluations of the social system by influencing how they perceive their social context, thereby advancing understanding of the broader psychological consequences of such beliefs.
